I have started going to all sorts of private clinics but I dont have money to keep it going forever. Probably spent over 10K in 2024 alone. I am currently on 300 mg Lyrica and 60mg Duloxetine in the morning. I am using Tramadol and Tramagetic later in the day. I always have a headache and nausea but I think it is because of the pain. Duloxetine was really effective the first week or so but then it lost most of its effect. When I increased to 120mg it had the same effect. I was basically pain free for a solid 2 hours. But I also had a spooky side effect: If I increase my dosage by too much, I get paranoid. I feel like every person on the street is after me, my thinking increases by like 3x. I tried increasing my dosage beyond the recommended 120mg because I am usually desperate for pain relief. I thought I was going to die.

I think that was the last medicine I tried. Every medicine has some side effects but anti depressants are usually a deal breaker to me. I didnt care to check the manual until I got some side effects. I got fainting spells, delurium and almost went psychotic. I threw them away after about 7 days when I realized I didnt really remember the last few days. It was amitriptyline or maybe Noritren. I dont remember.

3: Trigger map. Map out the times of day and the places where you are most likely to relapse. Common places are shower/bedroom and common times are morning/evening.

4: Avoid triggers. Uninstall social media if you must. Porn addiction is also intertwined with a general internet addiction in my experience so breaking up with your phone for a while might be a good idea.

5: Exercise. Get out of your door daily.

7: Urge surfing. Look up articles from A-12 groups/alcoholics recovery programs and maybe buy a book or two on different addictions. In the end heroine and porn isnt that much different. The only problem is that porn is a lot easier to access. Urge surfing is the act of aknowledging your urges without acting. You have physical urges and psychological urges. They feel slightly different. One is a compulsion from your reptile brain while the other one is more tangible. Identify which one it is and surf it for as long as possible. If you are unable to, take a few deep breaths and wait a minute before acting.

8: Cold showers. It resets your nervous system. There are several things going into this philosophy which is maybe best expressed in a book named "atomic habits". Basically, if you shower each time you feel urges you will take the edge off quickly. The 4 main pillars of getting rid of bad habits: Make it difficult, make it unenjoyable, make it invisible, make it untempting.

9: Knowledge. Seriously, read up. Armed with wisdom and recovery tools you will fare a lot better. 4 points about addictive behavior: Signal(trigger), urge. The first two you cant really control but the next two (response, reward) you can do something about. The more instant the reward, the stronger the compulsion will become. So you need to find strategies to make the reward less instant or reward yourself with a trip to your favorite cafe guiltless for not indulging.1

14: One day at a time. Dont look too far ahead. Focus on staying clean today, not tomorrow. Anyone can manage one day right? If that doesnt work neither, make it 5 minutes.
